title: Learned Routing of Latent State Between LLM Agents
kicker: Doctoral Research Direction · Multi-Agent Language Models
tools: PyTorch · Hugging Face Transformers · vLLM · Qwen3 / Qwen3.5 · Slurm on the OSU (Oregon State University) cluster · W&B (Weights & Biases)
blurb: Can LLM agents share internal state instead of text? Passing KV caches does carry information (91% vs 92% for text), but does not beat a single agent.
long: LLM (large language model) agents usually talk in text, which every recipient must re-read. Agents on the same model could instead pass internal state such as the KV cache. My NSF GRFP (National Science Foundation Graduate Research Fellowship Program) proposal is a manager that learns which compact summaries each agent should receive.

Audit. I reproduced LatentMAS (a published latent multi-agent method) on Qwen3-4B, bit-identical to the official code. The latent team ties a single agent, while a text team gains 3.4 and 2.4 points. Swapping in another question's cache costs 4.0 and 6.2 points, so information does cross; it just does not help when the receiver can solve the problem alone.

Split-information probe. When only the sender has the facts, the right cache scores 91%, text 92%, and a wrong or missing cache 0%. The cache message is about 61,000× larger than the text, which is the gap the proposal's learned summaries aim to close. I am writing up the audit as a paper.
highlights: LatentMAS (latent multi-agent system) reproduction on Qwen3-4B, bit-identical to the official code
Latent team ties a single agent: +0.1 / −0.2 points
Wrong cache costs 4.0 / 6.2 points: content does cross
Split probe: right cache 91%, text 92%, wrong or no cache 0%
Latent sender 19× faster, 2.4× fewer total FLOPs (floating-point operations), 61,000× larger message
note: Code private · paper draft in progress
